title: Catch-Up Drafts after a Returned Storage Unit Bank Draft: Bluegate AutoPay Authorization Tenant Approval Card
content:
**Terms.** A tenant whose storage unit AutoPay draft on a bank account under the Bluegate AutoPay Authorization was returned unpaid for insufficient or uncollected funds, and whose returned entry may not be presented again, may approve on a recorded call a one-time catch-up draft from the same account for that due date, on an authorization in active status. The approval is recorded on the authorization's notice history as a varying-amount notice for the returned due date stating the unit catch-up amount. A unit catch-up the tenant approves for a stated amount on a recorded call is a single entry authorized for that exact amount, so it is not held for the method's varying-amount notice period and runs on the next banking day.

| Condition | Required |
|---|---|
| Agreement drafted | A storage unit agreement |
| Draft returned | A bank-account draft returned unpaid for insufficient or uncollected funds |
| Returned entry | May not be presented again |
| Authorization status | Active |
| Who approves, and how | The tenant, on a recorded call |
| What is recorded | A varying-amount notice on the authorization's notice history, for the returned due date, stating the unit catch-up amount |
| When the catch-up runs | The next banking day, with no notice period |

## The approval tool

**Capability.** `approve_unit_returned_draft_catchup_31270510` lets the tenant, in person, approve a one-time catch-up draft on a storage unit AutoPay authorization for a rent due date whose bank-account draft came back unpaid. One call records, on that authorization's notice history, a new varying-amount notice dated today carrying the due date the catch-up concerns and the exact dollar amount the tenant approves to be drafted from the bank account on file. Nothing else on the authorization or on the rental agreement changes.

**How it is invoked.** It is the tenant's own tool: the agent unlocks `approve_unit_returned_draft_catchup_31270510` and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it.

**Parameters.**

- `autopay_id` — the AutoPay authorization number of the storage unit authorization the catch-up is drafted under, as shown in the AutoPay authorization lookup.
- `notice_type` — the kind of notice record written, one of:
- `varying_amount_notice` — the record states an amount to be drafted or charged for one due date; this is the kind this action records.
- `card_expiry_reminder` — a reminder that the card on file is about to expire, carrying no amount.
- `draft_failure_notice` — word that a draft for a due date failed, carrying no amount.
- `suspension_notice` — word that the authorization has been suspended, carrying no amount.
- `related_due_date` — the rent due date whose returned draft the catch-up concerns, written YYYY-MM-DD as a calendar date with no time and no time zone.
- `approved_amount` — the catch-up amount the tenant approves, in US dollars as a positive decimal number with exactly 2 decimal places (for example 123.45); stored rounded half-to-even to the cent.

**Return.** A text receipt of the form "Catch-up approval <reference> recorded on AutoPay <authorization number>: <amount> USD for due date <due date>, approved <date>.", the reference being the new notice reference beginning with apn_, the amount the stored amount with 2 decimals, and both dates written YYYY-MM-DD, the approval date being today. A receipt in this form means the approval is on record; the tenant receives the confirmation reference and can see the approved amount and due date on the authorization's notice history.
